seoTitle: How to Use Zapier with Microsoft Excel (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Connect Microsoft Excel to Zapier to automatically add rows, update cells, and sync spreadsheet data across your business apps.
intro: Keeping Excel data current across multiple apps usually means manual entry, which doesn't scale. This guide shows how to connect Microsoft Excel to Zapier, authenticate through Microsoft 365, and configure triggers or actions so new rows and updates flow automatically between Excel and other tools.

steps.heading: Create a new Zap
steps.body: Open the Zapier dashboard and start a new workflow.

steps.heading: Select Microsoft Excel
steps.body: Choose Excel from the app directory and review the available trigger or action events.

steps.heading: Authenticate your Microsoft account
steps.body: Sign in and grant the required OneDrive permissions safely.

steps.heading: Select your storage location and table
steps.body: Choose your target storage location, spreadsheet file, and specific table layout.

steps.heading: Fetch and test sample data
steps.body: Pull fresh row sample data to confirm your fields map correctly.

steps.heading: Map data and run a test
steps.body: Add an action step to map Excel fields to a second app, then run an end-to-end test to verify new row generation.

faq.question: Why should I format my data as an Excel Table?
faq.answer: Formatting your data as an official Table helps ensure error-free automated mapping when Zapier reads or writes rows.

faq.question: Can Zapier both read from and write to Excel?
faq.answer: Yes, Excel can serve as either a trigger, watching for new or updated rows, or an action, creating or updating rows automatically.

faq.question: Do I need OneDrive to connect Excel to Zapier?
faq.answer: Yes, the integration authenticates through your Microsoft 365 or OneDrive account to access your spreadsheet files.

faq.question: How do I confirm the connection is working?
faq.answer: Fetch fresh sample row data during setup and run an end-to-end test to verify new row generation inside Excel Online.
